dedupe_keys.name: usgs pedestrian evacuation analyst tool peat arcgis pro toolbox for on foot evacuation travel time modelling from tsunami flash flood or lahar zones

description: The Pedestrian Evacuation Analyst Tool (PEAT) is a USGS ArcGIS Pro toolbox (Jones 2024, v1.0.0, DOI 10.5066/P1WACACF) whose source is on code.usgs.gov. Contents: it estimates how long it would take someone to walk out of a hazard zone threatened by a sudden event such as a tsunami, flash flood or volcanic lahar, accounting for elevation change and land cover along the way; tools cover data preprocessing, the evacuation model that makes travel-time maps, and further analyses of vertical evacuation structures and evacuation pathways. Producer: USGS Western Geographic Science Center (author Jeanne Jones). Coverage: any study area for which the user supplies data such as a digital elevation model and land cover. Format and access: the zipped toolbox and a 19-page user guide are on ScienceBase; the Python source is on code.usgs.gov. Licence: The Unlicense (repository licence). Caveats: it requires Esri ArcGIS Pro; distance and flow accumulation steps can take minutes to an hour on large areas, and local storage is recommended. Simulation uses: evacuation travel-time and shelter siting analysis for emergency response and climate adaptation planning, and inputs to agent-based evacuation models.
